$comment: THIS IS AN OPEN P0-06 CONTROL GAP, AND IT IS DELIBERATE.
The floor is the value the live ruleset may not drop below. The target is the value
P0-06 wants. They differ because the repository has exactly ONE account with any
access at all - lacreativodesign, the owner, admin - and that account is the author
of every pull request. GitHub does not let a pull request author approve their own
pull request, so raising the live count to 1 today would not add a review: it would
stop anything merging, including the pull request that would undo it.
So the count stays 0 until an independent reviewer exists. Closing the gap is a
two-step owner action, in this order, never the second alone:
1. grant a second human WRITE access to the repository;
2. set required_approving_review_count to 1 AND set certifiedFloor to 1 here.
gapOpen is what keeps step 2 honest. The certification test refuses to let gapOpen go
false while certifiedFloor is still 0, so the gap cannot be closed on paper alone.

GitHub Actions - the `dependency-security` job in
.github/workflows/dependency-security.yml, added by PR #61 and merged to main on
2026-09-17 at 632f5daf6e5981dd610b59199c7230f38b8cd2c0. It runs `npm ci` then
`npm run security:audit`, which is `npm audit --audit-level=high`, so it fails on ANY
high or critical advisory across the whole lockfile including dev dependencies.
It is LIVE, not future work: the owner added it to ruleset 23581080 as a second
required status check, and it ran green on main after the merge (run 35264726041,
job 105348912555). PR #61 brought the repository to 0 critical and 0 high.
The workflow is deliberately NOT path-filtered. A required check that is skipped for
pull requests touching unrelated files leaves GitHub waiting on it forever, which
would block every such merge - the same dead-required-check failure mode this
certification checks for elsewhere.
Integration id 15368 is GitHub Actions and is pinned for the same reason as Vercel.
A check called `dependency-security` posted by anything else does not satisfy this.
BOTH of these are required on the live ruleset, and both were read back from
GET /repos/lacreativodesign/bizosto-website/rulesets/23581080 on 2026-09-17. The live
required_status_checks list contains exactly these two contexts and no others.
Losing either one is P0-06 drift, and so is re-pointing either at a different
integration. The contract is DIRECTIONAL, so the owner may add further required checks
without failing this record - but these two may never disappear.
